subject: Intermittent large-packet drops on Medicor private link — transient MTU / NAT interaction
messages:
From: Adam Lewis <adam.lewis@medicor.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@medicor.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity — intermittent large-packet failures

Hannah,

We started seeing spikes of 502 and failed uploads to your private gateway this morning during a backup window. The problem shows up for ~15-30s and then clears; it’s happening several times an hour. Our app logs show TLS connection resets and truncated payloads.

We captured a tcpdump on our side and attached it (medicor_diag_20260714_tcpdump.pcapng). Preliminary note from our infra: MSS/MTU probes look fine from the app-side, but there are lots of retransmits when payloads exceed ~1400 bytes. Can Redwood check the VPC edge and NAT behavior on the private gateway?

We’re on a dedicated private deployment (VPC peering + on-prem overlay). Happy to hop on a quick triage call.

—Adam
Adam Lewis
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Medicor Health
adam.lewis@medicor.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Adam Lewis <adam.lewis@medicor.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:08:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity — intermittent large-packet failures

Adam / team — I pulled the pcap and did a quick triage. Notes below (short form) — full dump attached as mtu-trace-outputs.txt.

Observations:
- Repro window: 2026-07-14 08:46:12 -0700 to 08:46:47 (matches your notes).
- SYN completes and TLS handshake starts, then bursts of Dup ACKs and retransmits when the client pushes >1400B segments.
- I see ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages being generated by an intermediate hop (TTL 6 -> hop responding), but the DF flag is set on packets from the client. That implies path MTU discovery kicked in but an intermediary cannot fragment and is signaling smaller MTU.
- On a few traces there are matching packets where source port translation changes mid-stream (NAT rebind) — likely from a load-balancer performing SNAT failover (ephemeral port switch). When NAT changes and packets are large, packets drop until flow re-establishes.

Hypothesis: transient MTU inference downshift + an intermittent SNAT rebind at our edge (or partner transit) correlates to the ~15-30s windows. The rebind causes out-of-state packets; combined with DF set and an intermediary reporting smaller MTU results in truncated payloads and resets.

Immediate asks for Medicor:
- Can you confirm the client applications set DF? (Some libs do by default.)
- Can you share output of "ip route get <gateway-ip>" and an mtr/traceroute during a repro window?

What I plan on our side:
- Check gateway NAT logs for port rebinds around the timestamps (karthik, can you pull the NAT logs & kernel dmesg for that timeframe?).
- Validate per-route MTU configs on the private edge, and confirm we don’t have an intermediate device with MTU <1500 on the path.

I’m attaching the key pcap excerpts and a short parsed output. If both sides confirm DF + SNAT rebind events, next step is to coordinate a short rolling rule to keep ephemeral SNAT port ranges sticky for Medicor source subnets while we narrow root cause.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

(attachment: mtu-trace-outputs.txt)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Lewis <adam.lewis@medicor.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity — intermittent large-packet failures

Adam — thanks for the patience and for the pcap. We pulled gateway NAT logs and saw two brief SNAT handovers coincident with your timestamps (2026-07-14T08:46:13Z and 2026-07-14T09:12:40Z). Those handovers were caused by our autoscaling placement moving a terminating worker (short-lived) due to a burst. During the handover the ephemeral port mapping momentarily fell out of the fast-path and packets with the original 5-tuple were treated as invalid; combined with the DF+ICMP fragmentation behavior you described leads to the symptoms you saw.

Temporary mitigations applied (effective immediately):
- Sticky SNAT mapping enabled for Medicor /28 source block for 60s to avoid mid-session rebinds.
- Increased default path MTU probe frequency on the gateway so we recover faster when an intermediary changes.

Longer-term actions:
- Karthik will open NET-8472 to track a code change to ensure SNAT handovers preserve 5-tuple state during worker transitions.
- We’ll schedule a joint failover test (no-app window) to validate the sticky mapping reduces your observed resets. Proposed slot: Thu 2026-07-16 03:00-03:30 UTC. Please confirm if that works for Medicor.

Adam — can you run a small synthetic after-hours test (curl PUT with 2MB payload) and share timestamps so we can verify post-mitigation behavior? If you’d prefer, we’ll run the test from our side against a test endpoint in your environment.

If the sticky rule does not eliminate the blips we’ll move to an in-line NAT state-sync for the pool (longer effort).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
